title: DSE — Office Workstation Setup
blurb: How to set up your chair, screen and keyboard, and work habits that prevent aches and eye strain.
siteNotes: Who arranges a workstation assessment and how to ask for one
Whether footrests and other equipment are available
legalNotes: Display screen equipment is covered by the Health and Safety (Display Screen Equipment) Regulations 1992. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1992/2792 (from general knowledge; not re-checked this session).

CHECK: the trainer's answer sheet for question 4 marks "Raised high" as correct, which contradicts the trainer text (forearms roughly horizontal). This session uses "Roughly horizontal" as the right answer; please confirm the answer sheet is a typo.

cards.title: DSE — Office Workstation Setup
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- adjust your chair and posture
- position your screen, keyboard and mouse
- take breaks and report discomfort

cards.title: A few adjustments, no cost
cards.body: If you spend time at a computer for bookings, admin, emails or rotas, how you set up your workstation matters. Poorly set up display screen equipment (DSE) can lead to back, neck and shoulder aches, wrist problems and eye strain over time.

cards.title: Start with your chair
cards.body: Adjust it so your forearms are roughly horizontal when typing and your feet are flat on the floor, using a footrest if they do not reach. Sit back so your lower back is supported, and relax your shoulders rather than hunching them up around your ears.

items.title: Feet
items.text: Flat on the floor or a footrest.

cards.title: Screen, wrists, mouse
cards.body: Position the screen about an arm's length away, with the top roughly at eye level so you are not craning your neck up or down. Keep your wrists straight and relaxed while typing and using the mouse.

left.title: Do
items: Top of the screen at eye level

right.title: Do not
items: Crane your neck up or down
Rest wrists on a hard edge

cards.title: Do not hold one position
cards.body: Even a perfect setup is not meant to be held rigidly for hours. Take regular short breaks, change position, and look away into the distance now and then to rest your eyes. If you get persistent aches or discomfort, report it so your workstation can be assessed and adjusted.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Forearms roughly horizontal, feet flat, lower back supported
- Screen an arm's length away, top at eye level
- Wrists straight and relaxed
- Take regular breaks and change position
- Report persistent aches so your workstation can be assessed

cards.why: DSE means display screen equipment, such as the computer and screen you use for bookings, admin and emails.
Position the screen about an arm's length away.

cards.q: The top of your screen should be roughly at eye level.
cards.why: That avoids craning your neck up or down.

cards.q: When typing, your forearms should be…
cards.why: Adjust the chair so your forearms are roughly horizontal when typing.

cards.q: Your feet should be flat on the floor (or on a footrest).
cards.why: Use a footrest if your feet do not reach.

cards.q: Which of these should you do regularly, even with a good setup?
options: Lean in closer to the screen
Work through without stopping to stay focused
Take short breaks and look into the distance
Raise your chair as high as it goes
cards.why: Take regular short breaks, change position and look into the distance to rest your eyes.

cards.q: Wrists should be kept straight and relaxed while typing.
cards.why: Avoid bending them up or resting them on a hard edge.

cards.q: Persistent aches or discomfort should be…
options: Endured until they pass of their own accord
Fixed by working in much shorter stints
Ignored until they get worse over time
Reported so the workstation can be assessed
cards.why: Report it so your workstation can be assessed and adjusted.

cards.q: A poor workstation setup can cause aches and eye strain over time.
cards.why: Back, neck and shoulder aches, wrist problems and eye strain can all build up.

cards.q: You should hunch your shoulders up while working.
cards.why: Relax your shoulders rather than hunching them up around your ears.
